email.body1:
Sean, saw SIS launched the AI-powered SIS Scribe at ASCA and marked 30 years serving over 2,900 surgical facilities.

A new AI product across a base that size usually opens more in-market accounts than the team can personally cover, and that whitespace cools fast. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for SIS off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Sean, quick follow-up for SIS.

Launching a new product into an installed base means cross-sell demand that jumps faster than headcount can. Most teams cannot say how many meetings they need to book to convert it, so the gap shows up late in the quarter.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings SIS needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Sean, last bit of proof for SIS.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how SIS's reply rate likely compares to other healthcare software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I will walk you through it?
